title: Mobile-based approach bias modification versus pseudomodification for the reduction of problematic internet use: A randomized controlled pilot study
summary:
Background
Many adolescents and young adults use the internet very intensively. For some of those affected, this leads to problems in everyday life, such as difficulty concentrating, conflicts in their social environment, or a loss of control over their own usage time. Researchers believe that automatic habits play an important role. These include the unconscious tendency to quickly turn to internet-related stimuli.

Research question
The study investigates whether training on a smartphone can help to change these automatic habits and thereby reduce problematic internet use. It examines whether a special training program is more effective than a comparable exercise program without a targeted training mechanism.

Methodology
The study is open to adolescents and young adults aged 16 to 25 who exhibit increased problematic internet use. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups use a training program on their smartphones several times a day over a period of three weeks. In one group, internet-related content is repeatedly linked to an “avoidance gesture,” while everyday offline activities are linked to an “approach gesture.” This is intended to change automatic reactions. In the comparison group, the reaction gestures are performed without such a targeted training principle.

Before the start, immediately after completing the training, and three months later, participants answer online questionnaires about their internet use and well-being. In addition, reaction tasks are performed to measure automatic habits in dealing with internet stimuli. The study is conducted entirely online, so no in-person appointments are necessary.

interventions.name:
Intervention: Mobile-based Approach-Avoidance Task (AAT) training to modify internet-related approach bias
- Web-based implementation in the browser of the participant's own smartphone using the touchscreen
- Systematic pairing of Internet-related stimuli with avoidance gestures (i.e., swiping awa

Control condition: Structurally identical pseudo-modification
- No systematic pairing of stimulus type and response gestures
- 2 blocks of 30 trials with alternating instructions per training session

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
CIUS sum score ≥ 30
Ownership of a smartphone with internet access
Sufficient German language skills
Exclusion criteria:
None
